channel.title: Kyunolab Mystery Archive
channel.description: Legends, folklore, mysteries, and strange tales.

item.title: Black Shuck Folklore: East Anglian Ghost Dog, Red Eyes, and the Roadside Omen That Keeps Returning
item.description: Black Shuck follows the East Anglian black dog folklore figure remembered as a large spectral hound, an omen, and a presence on roads, coasts, churches, and lonely paths.

item.title: Max Headroom Signal Hijacking: Broadcast Intrusion, Masked Figure, and the Television Night That Became Internet Memory
item.description: Max Headroom Signal Hijacking follows the 1987 Chicago broadcast signal intrusion in which a masked figure interrupted television programming and left a real recorded incident that later became internet folklore.

item.title: Yuki-onna Folklore: Snow Woman, Winter Road, and the Beauty That Arrives With Cold Silence
item.description: Yuki-onna follows the Japanese snow-woman figure remembered through winter encounters, cold beauty, mercy, threat, and stories where the snow itself seems to take human form.

item.title: Golem of Prague Folklore: Clay Protector, Sacred Letters, and the Created Guardian That Could Not Stay Simple
item.description: Golem of Prague follows the Jewish folklore tradition of a clay figure associated with Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague, protection, sacred words, and the danger of a created servant.

item.title: Roswell UFO Incident: Debris Recovery, Official Explanations, and the Crash Story That Would Not Stay Closed
item.description: Roswell UFO Incident follows the 1947 Roswell incident remembered through recovered debris, changing explanations, UFO belief, military secrecy, and decades of public retelling.

item.title: Crop Circles Mystery: Flattened Fields, Hoax Claims, and the Pattern That Made Farmland Look Signaled
item.description: Crop Circles follows the recurring field patterns made in crops, remembered through hoaxes, unexplained claims, aerial images, and debates over how a field becomes a message.

item.title: Killer in the Backseat Urban Legend: Headlight Warning, Hidden Passenger, and the Car That Was Not Empty
item.description: Killer in the Backseat follows the urban legend in which a driver is followed or warned because a dangerous stranger is hiding in the back seat of the car.

item.title: Kuchisake-onna Legend: Slit-Mouthed Woman, Masked Question, and the Street Encounter That Became Modern Fear
item.description: Kuchisake-onna follows the Japanese urban legend of a masked woman who asks whether she is beautiful before revealing a slit mouth and turning the answer into danger.

item.title: Icarus and Daedalus Myth: Wax Wings, Prison Escape, and the Fall That Made Warning Visible
item.description: Icarus and Daedalus follows the Greek myth of Daedalus building wings from feathers and wax, Icarus flying too close to the sun, and the fall that turns escape into warning.

item.title: Orion Constellation Myth: Hunter in the Sky, Scorpion Memory, and the Stars That Keep the Chase
item.description: Orion Constellation Myth follows the Greek hunter Orion remembered in the night sky, often linked with Artemis, the scorpion, and the seasonal chase among constellations.

item.title: Tunguska Event Mystery: Siberian Blast, Flattened Forest, and the Explosion Without a Crater
item.description: The Tunguska event remains one of the clearest examples of a real historical mystery: a vast Siberian blast, a flattened forest, eyewitness reports, scientific surveys, and no ordinary impact crater.

item.title: Flannan Isles Lighthouse Mystery: Missing Keepers, Empty Station, and the Sea Record That Stayed Open
item.description: The Flannan Isles lighthouse mystery follows the disappearance of three keepers from a remote Scottish lighthouse and the unsettling gap between official record, sea weather, and legend.

item.title: Trojan Horse Legend: Hidden Soldiers, Wooden Gift, and the Object That Opened a City
item.description: The Trojan Horse legend follows the wooden gift that entered Troy, the hidden soldiers associated with it, and the lasting warning about victory disguised as surrender.

item.title: Mjolnir: Returning Weapon, Thunder Sign, and the Object That Carries Protection
item.description: Mjolnir is followed as a Norse mythic object: a returning thunder weapon, a protective sign, and a compact symbol whose meaning reaches beyond battle.

item.title: Mount Olympus: Greek Divine Home, Clouded Summit, and the Place Where Gods Look Down
item.description: Mount Olympus is remembered as the mythic home of the Greek gods, a high place where weather, power, distance, and divine politics gathered above the human world.

item.title: Valhalla: Odin Hall, Chosen Warriors, and the Norse Place Waiting for Battle Again
item.description: Valhalla is remembered as Odin's hall for chosen warriors, a Norse afterlife image where battle, honor, death, feast, and final destiny meet.

item.title: Bioluminescent Bay Phenomenon: Glowing Water, Tiny Organisms, and the Shore That Lights Up at Night
item.description: Bioluminescent bays are real glowing-water phenomena where tiny organisms, darkness, motion, and sheltered coastal conditions make the shoreline seem to light from within.

item.title: Catatumbo Lightning: Lake Maracaibo Storms, Night Flashes, and the Sky That Keeps Returning
item.description: Catatumbo lightning is remembered for frequent night flashes near Lake Maracaibo, where geography, storms, and local memory turned weather into a recurring natural spectacle.

item.title: Tantalus Punishment Myth: Forbidden Feast, Water, Fruit, and Desire Kept Just Out of Reach
item.description: The punishment of Tantalus is remembered as a Greek myth of forbidden closeness: water below, fruit above, desire everywhere, and relief always out of reach.

item.title: Sisyphus and the Boulder: Endless Labor, Divine Punishment, and the Hill That Never Ends
item.description: Sisyphus and the boulder is remembered as a Greek myth of endless labor, divine punishment, repetition, cleverness, and the hill that refuses completion.
